claims.sentence: 103 of 275 courses state a grading scale (letter grade with a range of points)
The other 172 do not
The most common scale is A 90-100, B 75-89, C 60-74, D 0-59
54 of the 103 courses with a scale use it (52%)
The other 49 courses use 21 different scales
No other scale is used by more than 6 courses

Across all 103 courses that state a scale, the lowest points that earn grade A are: 90 in 60 courses; 85 in 22 courses; 80 in 12 courses; 92 in 2 courses; 136 in 1 courses; 95 in 1 courses; 96 in 1 courses; 104 in 1 courses; 84 in 1 courses; 86 in 1 courses

Across all 103 courses that state a scale, the lowest points that earn grade B are: 75 in 67 courses; 70 in 13 courses; 80 in 6 courses; 60 in 6 courses; 65 in 6 courses; 102 in 1 courses; 66 in 1 courses; 84 in 1 courses; 72 in 1 courses; 71 in 1 courses

Across all 103 courses that state a scale, the lowest points that earn grade C are: 60 in 70 courses; 50 in 12 courses; 40 in 6 courses; 65 in 3 courses; 55 in 3 courses; 56 in 2 courses; 70 in 2 courses; 51 in 2 courses; 68 in 1 courses; 45 in 1 courses
Across all 103 courses that state a scale, the lowest points that earn grade D are: 0 in 102 courses
2 course(s) give the ranges in raw points, not out of 100 (the top of grade A is above 100)
Courses with a scale by programme level are: BSc 56, MSc 40, other programs 7
Of the 56 BSc courses with a scale, 31 use the most common scale
Of the 40 MSc courses with a scale, 17 use the most common scale
Of the 7 other programs courses with a scale, 6 use the most common scale
The University has established rules for translating letter designations into the assessment system «excellent», «good», «satisfactory», «fail», «pass», «fail» (five-point scale)
The mapping is: A is «Excellent»; B is «Good»; C is «Satisfactory»; D is «Fail»; P is «Passed»; F is «Fail»
Results of interim assessment A, B, C and P are positive and cannot be retaken for improvement, except as specified in p. 6.1 of this Regulation
Results of interim assessment D and F are unsatisfactory results
Teaching staff member can use during teaching process may use alternative to established at University grading systems

In this case grading system, criteria of evaluation and conversion rules are specified in discipline (module) syllabuses, internships programs and communicated to students in the University's electronic educational environment
The evidence leaves open the specific conversion rules for the 49 courses that do not use the most common scale, as they use 21 different scales
The evidence does not specify the criteria for the "except as specified in p. 6.1" exception for retaking assessments
The evidence does not provide the specific syllabus content for the alternative grading systems used by teaching staff
The evidence does not explain the discrepancy in the scale A 85-100, B 75-85, C 60-74, D 0-59 where B and C ranges overlap or are adjacent in a non-standard way compared to the most common scale
The evidence does not clarify why 2 courses use raw points above 100
The evidence does not specify the content of the 172 courses that do not state a grading scale
